column1: # MARKER CLASSES -- the family a marker belongs to, and what that family looks
# like by default.
# A row in markers.tsv names its class; the class supplies the default SHAPE and
# COLOUR, and the row overrides either one.
# ADDING A MARKER is a row in markers.tsv. ADDING A WHOLE FAMILY is a row here.
# Neither is a code change and neither is a CSS change -- the class colour is
# emitted as generated CSS by docrender/markers.py.
# COLUMNS
# class    the token a markers.tsv row names
# shape    default shape for the family: box - plain - strike - soft
# color    default colour: any token from EITHER colour table, or a literal
#          hex/oklch
# wash     BOX SHAPES ONLY. How much of the marker's own colour tints the chip
#          behind the text, as a percentage. BLANK inherits the 10% baked into
#          the `.dr-mark--box` fallback, so every family that predates this
#          column renders byte-identically.
# label    what this family MEANS. For the reader of this file and the report.
# WHY CLASSES EXIST (DL J7, 2026-08-04). Every marker used to be a confidence
# claim, and that narrowness was the feature: you can ask "what is unconfirmed
# across this whole site" only while every row answers the same question. When
# terminology arrived it was nearly built as a SECOND, parallel family, because
# the table had no way to say which KIND a row was. Michael's ruling: it IS a
# marker, put it in markers, you have found CLASSES. The report groups by class,
# so the confidence question stays answerable however many terms a site marks.
# `wash` EXISTS BECAUSE THE HIGHLIGHT FAMILY NEEDED A FIFTH SHAPE AND DID NOT GET
# ONE (2026-08-07). The chip ALREADY had a tinted ground; 10% is simply below the
# level where a reader reads it as highlighting rather than as a border. A `mark`
# shape was rejected because "same shape, more tint" is not a new shape -- it is
# the same shape with a different number in it. The test that caught it: state
# the difference from `box` without using a number. You cannot.
# WASH AND COLOUR ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, so this is not a free dial. The chip text
# sits on a wash of ITSELF, so raising the wash lowers the contrast between the
# two. Measure the CHIP, not the page, and re-measure after changing this cell
# rather than only after changing `color`.
# `terminology` TAKES `accent-2`, NOT `accent-soft`, AND THE REASON IS A BUG WORTH
# REMEMBERING. `accent-soft` is a tinted GROUND, not a text colour -- on eos dark
# it measures 1.4:1 on the canvas. The validator refused it for two days (it read
# only the nine-token local table), everyone read the report line as "not vendored
# yet", and the fallback to body colour is the only reason nobody noticed the cell
# was ALSO wrong. A broken reference that degrades gracefully can hide a second,
# worse mistake underneath it.
# COLOUR COLLISIONS ONLY COUNT WHERE COLOUR CARRIES THE MEANING
# The rule here used to be: two callouts may share a token, two INLINE MARKERS
# may not, because they appear in the same sentence and only the paint tells them
# apart. STRUCK 2026-08-09 on Michael's ruling: *"i don't care if they're visually
# identical. the reporting tag is usually to be different. the front end would
# begin to look like skittles if everything had its own color at this point."*
# The corrected rule is narrower. A collision is a defect only where the COLOUR IS
# CARRYING THE MEANING. A reader separates `conf` from `gap` by paint, so those
# must stay apart. Nobody reads a `.calc` chip and asks how confident it is -- the
# TAG carries that, the report consumes the tag, and the paint only says "this is
# marked." The old rule was derived from ONE family type, where hue IS the
# semantics, and then stated about all of them.
# CONSEQUENCE: `layout` and `highlight` both take `accent` and differ only by wash
# (10% against 25%); `schema` and `terminology` both take `accent-2`. DELIBERATE.
# Do not "fix" either pair. If a reader ever genuinely needs to tell two apart and
# cannot, the answer is a different SHAPE or a different tag, never a new hue.
# THE FMP FAMILIES -- `layout`, `schema`, `alias`. Owner: FMP Fiona, 2026-08-09.
# These document a FileMaker solution in git. The membership test is FileMaker's
# OWN TWO HALVES:
#   layout   LAYOUT MODE. A button, a field, a portal, the layout itself.
#            Something you place on a screen. Met in prose, so it is boxed.
#   schema   THE MANAGE MENU. Manage > Database (calculations, relationships),
#            Manage > Scripts (scripts, triggers), Manage > Value Lists, and
#            globals. Met inside a table of fields, so it is plain -- a boxed
#            chip in every cell of a .tsv is a wall.
#   alias    NEITHER, because you can alias either one. A retired NAME pointing
#            at the live one.
# THIS TEST IS THE THIRD ONE WRITTEN TODAY AND THE FIRST THAT SURVIVES ITS OWN
# MEMBERSHIP. The first was "layout objects vs not-objects" -- killed by Michael
# in one line, *"the relationship is an object tho."* The second was "FileMaker has
# no surface that enumerates these, so this doc is the register" -- true of calcs,
# triggers and globals, and false of value lists the moment `.vl` arrived, because
# Manage > Value Lists is exactly such a surface. The third failed on SCRIPTS,
# which are not "how the data is shaped" by any honest reading.
# THE PATTERN IN ALL THREE FAILURES IS ONE THING: a definition was written from
# the rows that existed, and every one of those rows passed several tests at once,
# so nothing could tell the tests apart. A definition is only ever tested by the
# case that SPLITS it -- which means the next marker, not the current five.
# HONEST WRINKLE, STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER: `schema` is now the wider half
# and its name is the narrower word. A script is not a schema. The name is kept
# because it is already shipped and already in content, and because "the Manage
# menu" is not a word. If a fourth failure arrives, rename it then and say so.
# WHY TWO FAMILIES AND NOT ONE "fmp": one family answers "show me the FileMaker
# things," which nobody needs. Two answer "every relationship" and "every control"
# separately, and the report is only worth reading while each class answers ONE
# question. The build report is the entire return here -- it needed a TAG, never a
# hue.
# `alias` IS `was` ONE LAYER UP. `was` supersedes a VALUE; alias supersedes a
# NAME. It is a separate row rather than a reuse because it carries an ID: an
# alias RESOLVES to the live name (`[fkCal](@alias:table-workdays#calc-fkCalendar)`),
# so its link form is the primary one and the underline is honest. `text-soft`
# measures 6.31 dark / 5.45 light against its own 10% chip, clearing the 4.5 text
# floor in both schemes, and it reads quiet -- which is right for a name that is
# no longer the name.
# NOT BUILT, NAMED SO IT IS NOT RE-DISCOVERED: `tab` and `popover` were raised as
# `layout` candidates and DEFERRED by Michael on 2026-08-09. `portal` was deferred
# with them and then added anyway in the same session, because it was ALREADY
# TYPED on a live page and therefore already rendering as nothing -- the rule is
# add the marker when it is being reached for, and it was.
class
confidence
column5: how much to trust the value beside it

column1: terminology
column5: a defined term, with or without a page behind it

column1: highlight
column5: worth noticing. Says nothing about the value, only that Michael wanted your eye here

column1: layout
column5: FileMaker LAYOUT MODE -- something placed on a screen. Met in prose

column1: schema
column5: FileMaker's MANAGE MENU -- calculations, relationships, scripts, triggers, globals, value lists. Met inside a table

column1: alias
column5: a RETIRED NAME that points at the live one. Neither layout nor schema, because you can alias either
